title: CVA attack-lab scenario manifest
description: The one schema that CROSSES THE SEAT BOUNDARY TO THE ADVERSARY. ML-1, ML-2 and Crypto write scenarios against it, and the benchmark reads ground truth from it — so the `expect` block is not documentation, it is the answer key the bench scores against. A scenario without `seed` and `expect` cannot participate in either the reproducibility gate (same manifest + seed -> byte-identical corpus, twice, on two machines) or the detection matrix.

module.description: Which module's detectors this scenario is an answer key for.

attack_class.description: MUST be declared in core/taxonomy.py. The bench groups on it, so an undeclared or drifted string scores against nothing and the coverage row silently vanishes.

seed.description: The corpus is a function of this. backend_revised §2.9's gate is 'same manifest + seed -> byte-identical corpus, twice, on two machines' — which requires all three RNGs seeded, PYTHONHASHSEED set IN THE ENVIRONMENT (it is read at interpreter start, so setting it in-process is too late), and ORT threads pinned.

base.description: What the attack is applied TO. Held separate from the attack so a clean/attacked matched pair differs in exactly one thing.

poison_rate.description: The sweep axis that turns 'may miss adaptive attacks' into 'detects patch triggers at poison rate >= X%'.

fitness_gate.description: The lab REFUSES to emit an unfit corpus. A model that never learned and a 'backdoor' that never took are both worthless as test subjects — but so is a model at accuracy 1.000, which is why there is an UPPER bound too.

max_clean_acc.description: A DIFFICULTY gate, not just a fitness gate. An easy corpus does not under-test a margin-based detector, it INVERTS it: at accuracy 1.000 decision boundaries are degenerate, a minimal universal trigger is small for every class, and Neural Cleanse's premise — that one class is unusually reachable — collapses.

min_asr.description: attack success rate; a backdoor that did not take is not a backdoor

expect.description: The answer key. Detection rate AND FALSE-ALARM RATE are scored separately: a detector tuned only against attacks has no measured false-alarm rate, and the false-alarm column is what decides whether an analyst keeps reading.

ground_truth.description: Clean scenarios are REQUIRED, not optional. Without them there is no false-alarm denominator and every reported detection rate is unfalsifiable.

detected_by.description: Detectors expected to fire. An EXPECTED MISS belongs in `expected_misses` with a reason, not omitted quietly.

expected_misses.description: A declared blind spot, with the reason it is one BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by defect — e.g. Neural Cleanse optimises a small localised mask, so a SIG-family global sinusoidal overlay is outside its premise. That is a measured limitation for the coverage statement, and it is exactly the kind of declared blind spot the PS asks for three times.

contributor.description: For the mixed-contributor rollup gate: the guilty contributor must rank FIRST.

holdout_family.description: Which family this belongs to for HELD-OUT-FAMILY calibration. A threshold fitted on the data it is reported against is not a result; the discipline is calibrate on one family, evaluate on another, and say which was which.

artefact_sha256.description: Recorded after generation so the reproducibility claim is checkable rather than asserted.
